filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning to confirm CUA requirements for laundromat removal under Section 202.12 and discuss likely conditions.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Explain that the project is a limited-service restaurant converting a former laundromat at 767 Bush St (RC-4 zoning), and that you understand Section 202.12 requires a CUA for this change of use. Ask which findings and conditions Planning will expect, whether neighborhood notification under Section 311 applies, and what evidence of public benefit or laundromat operator search will satisfy the Commission. Request guidance on how to frame the CUA application to address residential compatibility and the intent of the laundromat-protection ordinance.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the business registration within 30 days of forming the entity. Pay the tiered fee based on projected gross receipts ($55 minimum). The BAN is required by every other City department (Planning, DPH, DBI, SFPUC).
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Attend the Planning Commission hearing on the CUA, present the project, and respond to Commissioner questions and any public comment.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Arrive prepared to answer questions about hours of operation, noise management, waste and grease disposal, and how the restaurant serves the residential neighborhood. Acknowledge the loss of the laundromat and explain why the restaurant is a compatible and beneficial use: it will operate during daytime/early-evening hours, provide affordable meals for residents and workers, generate foot traffic that supports other local businesses, and maintain an active storefront in a high-density corridor. Commit to the good-neighbor policy and any conditions the Commission proposes (hours limits, no late entertainment, complaint hotline). If neighbors raise concerns, address them respectfully and offer to meet after the hearing to work out operational details.

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit application with DBI.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Pay the permit fees (percentage of construction valuation, typically $800–$15,000). Licensed subcontractors will pull separate electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits as needed.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

timeline_cost.notes: This range is the time to obtain the three approvals (CUA, health permit, building permit) when they are granted, not the time to a denial or withdrawal. The Conditional Use Authorization is the critical path: approximately 120–300 days from filing to approval including pre-application meeting, environmental review, neighborhood notification if required, Planning Commission hearing, and the 30-day appeal period. The building permit (14–120 days) and health permit (14–45 days) follow sequentially because DBI will not issue the building permit until the CUA is final, and DPH will not issue the health permit until construction and final inspection are complete. Government fees include CUA application (estimated $3,000–$3,500 based on typical 2023 rates, adjusted annually), building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction value), DPH plan check ($828–$2,500), health permit to operate ($470), business registration ($55–$700), entity formation ($70–$150), and small fees for EDD, fictitious business name, sign permit, and FOG program. This estimate excludes construction costs, architect fees, insurance, and any deposits. The 779 Bush St CUA (14 m away, filed November 2022 for a laundromat-to-bar conversion) has been pending with no decision as of the data cut-off, suggesting that laundromat-removal CUAs may face longer review or neighbor opposition; confirm the likely timeline at the pre-application meeting.

records_summary: 767 Bush St is in the RC-4 (Residential Commercial, High Density) zoning district where a restaurant is principally permitted on the ground floor as a Retail Sales and Service use. No prior permits or applications are on file at this address. The site sits in an extremely dense food and beverage corridor: 33 registered food or drink businesses and 26 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet, signaling high undue-concentration risk if alcohol were added later. The immediate block has seen consistent approvals for restaurant uses over the past decade, including two new restaurants with alcohol approved in May 2022 at 550 and 560 Powell (115 m away), both in RC-4 zoning.
